Ten hypotheses follow, mostly built on two patterns in the 98 experiments:

- **Edge 3 is the direct skip from input to output.** When it is `none`, the cell has no shortcut path. Edits that add a path or residual tend to gain much more then, especially on ImageNet16-120. Removing other paths then tends to hurt much more.
- **What the edit replaces matters.** Replacing a parameter-free op (`none` or `avg_pool_3x3`) with a conv or skip gives large gains. Removing an existing 3x3 conv on a key edge costs more than removing a weaker op.

Most hypotheses are supported by only one to five matched comparisons from the experiments, so they are well-motivated rather than established.
